title: CS enterprise ask harmonization and initial scope heuristic
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Create a repeatable, light-weight process and artifact set for Sales/CS to aggregate enterprise feature requests (non-bug), perform an initial harmonization/deduplication pass, and produce a first-pass scoping envelope that Product can action. Goal is to reduce noisy, inconsistent asks reaching PMs and to speed time-to-first-scope for high-value enterprise opportunities.
background: Over the last 9 months we've seen an increase in large accounts submitting overlapping feature asks via email, Slack, and support tickets. PMs are spending significant time normalizing asks before evaluation. Existing playbooks focus on backlog prioritization but lack a concrete inbound aggregation step for CS/Sales. This initiative is scoped to non-bug feature requests for enterprise customers (SaaS customers with contract value > $250k / year) and should integrate with our existing Linear intake and Confluence PRD templates.
acceptance_criteria: Sales/CS have a one-page intake template (Google Sheet + copyable email template) that enforces required metadata: customer, account ARR, problem statement, use case, expected MRR impact, timeline, data sensitivity, and preferred solution sketch.
A harmonization workflow (Slack workflow + weekly aggregator sheet) exists that groups similar asks and surfaces top 5 clusters per week to assigned PMs.
First-pass scope artifact: for each cluster PM receives a 1-paragraph value hypothesis, rough effort band (S/M/L) and suggested owner (PM or Solutions Eng) within 72 hours of cluster sync.
Measured reduction in PM normalization time by at least 40% in the first 6 weeks (tracked via PM time logs / intake dashboard).
Hand-off into product queue is consistent: clustered items create a Linear PM-epic with links to the intake sheet and any customer artifacts.

updates: 2026-02-20: Ticket created after Growth and CS call flagged increased fragmentation of enterprise asks.
2026-02-24: Draft intake template shared — initial feedback from AE: include 'likelihood to buy in next 90 days' checkbox. Added to template.
2026-02-27: Engineering feasibility sync — ENG-3482 to build Slack-to-sheet ingestion next sprint. No major blockers; rate limit concerns for high-volume channels noted.
2026-03-02: Pilot cohorts selected (East Coast AE pod, EU Strategic AE). Scheduled kickoff training for 2026-03-05.
2026-03-05: Kickoff runbook reviewed with AEs. Action: AEs to use sheet for all enterprise non-bug asks for pilot duration. Slack workflow deployed to a test channel.

2026-03-07: First weekly aggregator run produced 23 raw rows -> 6 clusters. PM quick-scope emails delivered within 40 hours for top two clusters. Early signal: two clusters map to existing roadmap epics.
2026-03-09: Feedback from Solutions Eng: request to add 'data ingress/egress requirements' field to template. Updated template and notified AEs.
Open question: Should legal/contract impact be captured in intake or left to post-scope review? Proposal: capture a binary 'contract change likely' field to minimize back-and-forth.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: AEs won't adopt new template during quota pressure. Mitigation: require template completion for any feature ask logged as 'enterprise' in the pilot pods; provide 15-minute onboarding and a short cheat-sheet.

Risk: High volume creates noise and noisy clusters. Mitigation: initial dedupe heuristics conservative — cluster only when two or more fields match (problem statement keywords, customer segment), escalate ambiguous rows to Solutions Eng for triage.
Risk: Security/regulatory asks require deeper review. Mitigation: add 'data sensitivity' and 'contract change likely' fields to filter early and add an automatic review tag for Security/Legal.
